summary: Round 1 (Oct 17) fixed issue 1. A live bundle's time_range.now_ms, which is also the default forecast start, is now the latest observation of the fire, and a satellite pass that saw nothing counts as one. The passes are VIIRS and MODIS active-fire granules from NASA CMR, counted only when confirmed: published at least 30 min before our FIRMS data of that satellite were fetched. The burned area stays at the last detection or perimeter (new optional time_range.last_detection_ms / last_pass_ms). The start stays at the last detection when CAL FIRE reports much more acreage than mapped, or when CMR is down. Live forecasts also hold the quiet perimeter (activity markers and a CAL FIRE containment minimum count), and when the start is a quiet pass the multiplier's decay is counted from the last activity. Henderson's forecast for Oct 17 evening went from 13,004 ac (old rule; 13,330 ac on the same data) to a held 3,228 ac, against CAL FIRE's 3,160 ac at 50 % containment. On 51 pseudo-live re-issues of past fires the quiet cases improved (total Sørensen 0.36 -> 0.67, error 4,954 -> 2,278 ac, median ratio 86x -> 2.6x). Also in round 1: issue 7 (CAL FIRE summaries now synced every live cycle), bounded live-forecast disk use, a test that walks every endpoint and file of the 8 real bundles (it found and fixed an aircraft HTTP 500), robustness tests, and a count-only secret scan (0 hits). Round 2 (Oct 18, known issue 1: small burning fires) found that the premise did not hold for Cooley. Its hot pixels are at the edge (median depth 105 m), not inside. CAL FIRE's 731.4 ac merely repeats the 13:06 PDT perimeter (730 ac), so Cooley's over-prediction is not established. Five alternatives were tested on the 32 calibration leads and the 51 pseudo-live issues: edge filters at 375/750 m, a 500/750 m activity radius, and growth-coincident detections only (with and without an edge filter). Edge filters barely matter. The smaller radius cost Eaton 0.012. Counting a detection only where it coincides with growth (a hot pixel on ground that burned more than 12 h earlier is burnout) improved every measure with no fire worse: hindcast growth Sørensen 0.422 -> 0.432 (Madre 0.353 -> 0.392); pseudo-live growth 0.227 -> 0.234 and error 6,932 -> 6,434 ac. That rule was adopted (FORECAST_ACTIVE_GROWTH_ONLY); the radius and edge settings are unchanged. No variant changes the small fires: the archive has almost no active small-fire issues (1 of 33 on a 2-hourly schedule), and their remaining over-prediction comes from spread from edges that crews had already stopped, which the model cannot represent. The live forecasts were republished through the API on 8711 with the new default (areas identical; holds unchanged). check_bundle shows 0 problems, and 518 backend tests pass (478 before round 1).

known_issues:
1 (high) Small fires that crews stop early are still over-predicted, and the archive cannot test the active case.
  - In pseudo-live quiet issues, Lidia and Camino average about 1,450 ac of forecast growth against about 50 ac observed. Of 33 two-hourly small-fire issues, only 1 is active (Camino: 1,696 ac vs 0).
  - The model has no suppression or initial attack; only the live CAL FIRE containment minimum stands in for it.
  - Cooley's apparent over-prediction (2,100 ac at +24 h vs CAL FIRE 731 ac) is NOT established: 731.4 ac repeats the 13:06 PDT perimeter, and VIIRS saw heat all around the edge at 13:24-15:52. Only the next mapped perimeter can verify it.
  - None of the rules tested in round 2 (edge filters, smaller radius, growth-only) changes the small fires; a fix would need a suppression or initial-attack model.

2 (medium) Forecast skill is moderate. Hindcast growth Sørensen is 0.432 (median growth ratio 1.85); pseudo-live it is 0.234 (ratio 2.66). Late growth is still over-predicted and the first hours of extreme runs under-predicted.

3 (medium) The pseudo-live evidence is a small, one-sided sample: 14 quiet issues, 9 of them from Lidia. Archived bundles hold no detections after end_ms and no low-confidence pixels, and the containment minimum cannot be hindcast.

4 (medium) A quiet pass only means no fire above the detection limit: thick cloud or smoke, swath-edge geometry or smouldering can hide a burning fire. The CAL FIRE acreage veto catches only growth already reported. A fully held perimeter means no modelled growth, not that the fire is out (the warning says so).
5 (medium) Passes are looked up at the fire's centroid, so a very large fire can lie partly outside a granule. MODIS passes count like VIIRS for the start time.

6 (low) A quiet fire's start moves forward only when a refresh runs (new detections, or every 3 h). It can trail the newest pass by up to about 3 h, plus 0.75-3 h of CMR publication latency and the 30 min confirmation margin.
7 (low) The containment minimum guesses where the contained lines are (the perimeter farthest from recent activity).
8 (low) Ensemble spread is narrow (weather-only members; p10-p90 2-4 % of area).
9 (low) The published historical hindcasts (validation 5.2) predate the growth-only rule; Madre's published run would improve if re-made.
10 (low) README 'Live forecasts' belongs to the readme agent; suggested text is in notes_for_integrator.
11 (low) fixture-demo and fixture-live keep the fx-001 'arrival before the start' note (fixture-only).
12 (low) adsb.lol is unreachable from this network; adsb.fi (non-commercial use only) answers instead.

README 'Live forecasts' paragraph (readme agent; it carries a verify note for this change). Suggested text:
Live forecasts start at the latest observation of the fire: its newest satellite detection or mapped perimeter, or a later satellite pass that looked at the fire and saw no new fire (checked against NASA's catalogue of VIIRS and MODIS passes). The burned area stays at the last mapped extent. A perimeter that stayed quiet for 12 hours is held, and at least CAL FIRE's contained share is held. A fully held perimeter means no modelled growth, not that the fire is out. Example, Oct 17, 2026: Henderson's old forecast started at its last detection (Oct 16, 14:48 PDT) and predicted about 13,000 acres for that evening. The new one starts at the latest pass (Oct 17, 15:50 PDT, 13 passes with no fire) and holds 3,228 acres; CAL FIRE reported 3,160 acres, 50 % contained.
